title: Reimbursement is conditioned on how the beneficiary runs the litigation, giving the funder influence over defense strategy
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.4.5 makes four duties binding "in the conduct of the litigation and as a condition of receiving reimbursement": act "honestly, consistently, and fairly" (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.5.1); "make an early assessment of the prospects of success and deal with claims promptly" (.4.5.2); "keep costs to a minimum and avoid reliance on technical defenses which have low probability of success" (.4.5.3); and "consider alternative dispute resolution (ADR) options at all times" (.4.5.4).

These are recognizable insurer cooperation clauses, and they solve a real moral-hazard problem: a defendant spending someone else's money has no reason to settle early, drop weak arguments, or economize.

The consequence, though, is that the funder acquires a say in the defense. "Avoid reliance on technical defenses which have low probability of success" is a strategic judgment normally made by counsel with the client's interests alone in view — and a technical defense with low odds may still be a defendant's best option when the alternative is an adverse merits finding. "Consider ADR at all times" leans toward settlement, which is cheaper for the fund but may mean accepting terms or admissions a contested defense would have avoided.

Since these are conditions of reimbursement rather than obligations owed to a client, the beneficiary bears the risk of disagreement: run the defense your lawyer recommends and Sky may decline to pay. Combined with the Lawyer Registry gate, Sky influences who defends the case and how it is fought — without being the client.
description: Good faith, early prospects assessment, minimizing cost, avoiding low-probability technical defenses and continuous ADR consideration are all conditions of receiving Fund money.
